calendar.impact: The wider group meets to set the 2027 production framework and baselines, resting on an independent capacity assessment that was completed on Nov 17 and has not been published.

changes.balance: The surplus pricing is three weeks old and the tape is pausing inside it on weekends and expiry weeks, while the traded Canadian strip tightens on deferred volume and the West Coast line runs at a record rate, which says the basin residual and the market still disagree and the market is the one trading.
changes.body: Brent Jan27 settled $92.57, up $0.59, and WTI Jan27 settled $83.41, up $0.97, on Friday (Reuters, Nov 20), with January taking over as the front month after December expired at $83.98. Brent finished the week down 3.41 percent, a third straight weekly loss, and the Brent prompt spread weakened on Friday. The factors on the board for the late gain are renewed strike worries on Iran, Thanksgiving short covering, and the day's tanker fire; which factor carried it is not established.
changes.conditional: A weekend incident that removes a named vessel or a measured flow print below the last gauge reprices the front against the surplus on Monday; a quiet weekend leaves the surplus pricing in charge into the Nov 29 OPEC+ meeting.
changes.delta: Friday settled higher, Brent up 59 cents and January WTI up 97 cents, and both benchmarks still closed a third straight weekly loss
changes.source: Reuters, Nov 20, 2026; Bloomberg via Rigzone, Nov 20, 2026
changes.title: Friday settled higher into the weekend, and the week still belongs to the surplus

changes.balance: The destination leg of the discount is now printing in the Gulf's own sour marker while the location spread stays orderly and the West Coast line runs at a record rate, which strengthens the read that the marginal heavy barrel is being discounted at destination and that the balance error sits in one of two named suspects, either the production estimates are too high or the egress capacity is too low.
changes.body: January WCS paper settled -$21.65 (ICE TMW settle, Nov 20), up $0.35, with February at -$21.40 on 435 lots and March at -$21.00 on 215 lots, a fourth straight tightening session. January Houston WCS paper settled -$14.00 (ICE ARV settle, Nov 20), which puts the January ARV to TMW spread at +$7.65. Mars fell from a $10 premium to a $4 discount against WTI in less than a month on a surge in heavy and sour supply from Canada, Venezuela and the Middle East (Bloomberg via Rigzone, Nov 20). The pipeline carrying oil sands crude to West Coast export markets is operating at a record 960 kb/d in November, with 34 vessels scheduled out of Westridge against 31 in October.
changes.conditional: A strip that holds its tightening through next week against the December allocation confirms the repricing; a Mars discount that keeps steepening while Hardisty holds would separate the destination leg from the basin leg entirely.
changes.delta: January WCS paper tightened 35 cents to -$21.65 with the January export spread at +$7.65, Mars swung to a $4 discount from a $10 premium in under a month, and West Coast flows are running at a record 960 kb/d
changes.source: ICE Report Center EOD, Nov 20, 2026; Bloomberg via Rigzone, Nov 20, 2026
changes.title: The strip tightened a fourth session, the Gulf sour premium vanished, and West Coast flows set a record

changes.balance: The incident tempo and the flow gauges still point in different directions: attacks are rising again near Khasab and over Riyadh while the strait gauge holds near half of pre-war and all-route regional oil has fallen back from its October peak, so the market is pricing returning barrels that the measured gauges only partly confirm.
changes.body: An outbound tanker was struck north of Khasab on Friday afternoon and caught fire, with no casualties reported (UKMTO Warning 214-26, Nov 20), the fourth strike in the area in five days, and early Saturday the coalition intercepted three ballistic missiles fired toward Riyadh. Crude through the strait itself ran at 8.5 million barrels a day in preliminary figures through Nov 16, about 50 percent of pre-war (Kpler via Associated Press, Nov 18), while oil moving by all routes out of the Middle East ran at 15.0 million barrels a day, about 64 percent of pre-war and down from 97 percent in October. Transits in the week ending Nov 18 fell 14.6 percent to 263, about 65 percent below pre-conflict levels.
changes.conditional: A fresh measured strait print materially below the Nov 16 gauge, or a confirmed loadings halt, reprices the front against the surplus; a print holding near 8.5 million barrels a day confirms the incident tempo is noise for deliverable supply at current bypass rates.
changes.delta: A fourth Khasab-area tanker strike landed Friday, three missiles were intercepted over Riyadh early Saturday, and the fresher strait gauge holds at about 50 percent of pre-war through Nov 16
changes.source: UKMTO Warning 214-26, Nov 20, 2026; Reuters, Nov 21, 2026; Kpler via Associated Press, Nov 18, 2026
changes.title: Another tanker was struck near Khasab, Riyadh was targeted again, and the strait gauge holds near half of pre-war
changes.vintage: Kpler media briefing via Associated Press, Nov 18, 2026, data to Nov 16

flags.body: December Mainline apportionment (Light 24 percent at Kerrobert, Heavy 17 percent at Kerrobert) is announced for December. The Cromer and Superior points for December were not retrievable in any public source. The traded differential strip tightened for a fourth straight session after the notice, with January WCS paper settling -$21.65, and the balance residual is qualified against that pricing rather than carried as a storage forecast.
flags.title: December apportionment: Light 24 and Heavy 17 at Kerrobert
flags.trigger: The Enbridge December apportionment percentages as published in the notice itself

flags.body: A fourth tanker strike in the Khasab area in five days landed on Friday and three ballistic missiles were intercepted over Riyadh early Saturday, with the JMIC threat level remaining SEVERE. The last measured strait clearance is 8.5 million barrels a day through Nov 16, about 50 percent of pre-war, while all-route Middle East oil ran at 15.0 million barrels a day, about 64 percent of pre-war and down from 97 percent in October. Wire lines that Hormuz shipments have returned to pre-war levels are not confirmed by these gauges. A confirmed measured flow print resolves which gauge the pricing should follow.
flags.title: Incident tempo rising into the weekend, and the strait gauge holds near half of pre-war
flags.trigger: A fresh measured clearance print from a tracker, or a confirmed loadings halt from an owner or UKMTO product

flags.body: The North Dakota Pipeline chloride disruption entered its eighth day on Saturday, with the 475 kb/d system curtailed since Nov 14, producers trucking Bakken crude to Dakota Access Pipeline delivery points on Friday, tanks filling and trucks in short supply, and force majeure declarations standing at Flint Hills Pine Bend and at MPLX. Enbridge has not confirmed a shut-in and no restart timeline has been published.
flags.title: North Dakota Pipeline chloride disruption on its eighth day, with no restart timeline
flags.trigger: An Enbridge statement on the disruption, or a reported restart of normal operations
